2024, revised review:

Since Covid-19 and lockdown, everything has gone downhill and become impersonal. As you will see from my previous review (2019), still left below, I didn't always think negatively about the practice.

Fortunately, I rarely need an appointment now, only for yearly pill check with a nurse, but on my last visit, I was directed to check-in via a screen - which many people do prefer to use. In doing so, I didn't see or speak to anyone until I saw the nurse (who was lovely, considerate and under). It was so quiet, not at all busy. No noise, hubbub. I felt like the only one in the building. I don't recall hearing a phone ringing.

There were approximately ten chairs - not the dozens which occupied the waiting room previously - and I took up one of them. I arrived just over five minutes early, checked in and waited for almost 30 minutes. Two other female patients arrived 10-15 minutes after me. During my wait, a name came on the screen to be buzzed in... for a man who wasn't even there!!

Eventually, I saw the nurse and she asked how long I had been waiting and if I checked in via the screen. I told her, she apologised and blamed the system for not working as expected.

Appointment booking wise via the website or app is redundant because you can't book to see a doctor. Everything is triaged by the team on receptionist, including telephone requests. If I wanted an appointment today I couldn't because: We have paused access to contact us online as we have reached capacity for the day.

Gone are the days of ringing up for a same day or next day appointment.

The world has opened back up since lockdowns, Woodlands Surgery - and many other practices - have not.

----

Previous review from approx 2019:

The waiting time for your preferred doctor is longer than necessary. For example, if you want an appointment for some time in November, you have to call at the very start of October (when the books are open). Even then you are not guaranteed an appointment (e.g. no availability or the doctor is on leave).

The practice is very popular and busy - but extremely overcrowded with patients.

I like that you can see some available appointments online for the doctors and nurses (i.e. blood pressure and phlebotomy), also, you can order repeat prescriptions. That can help and slightly ease the work on the receptionists by booking yourself in

The receptionists have always been polite and courteous to me. I have my preferred female doctor who has been a Godsend. I have been lucky to engage in a decent doctor/patient relationship with someone who I like and trust. For me, that is key.

Overall, the practice and staff are great but it is not without its
